study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study in Oslo, Norway. Patients were recruited from inpatient and outpatient clinics in the Oslo area, and healthy individuals were drawn from the national population registry in the same catchment area. MRI data were acquired on a single 1.5T Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata scanner.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study from October 27, 2004, to October 17, 2012." answer.TOP: normative model training/testing (healthy controls, 10-fold cross-validation) and clinical application (schizophrenia spectrum and bipolar disorder patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The TOP study provided both the healthy control group (n=256) for estimating the normative model under 10-fold cross-validation, and the clinical groups (218 schizophrenia spectrum, 190 bipolar disorder) to which the trained normative model was applied to quantify individual deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model trained on all data to patients."

model-1.model-name: VBM-based normative model (gray and white matter volumes)
model-1.train-phase: NR (10-fold cross-validation used; no separate fixed train split reported)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was estimated using gaussian process regression on VBM-derived gray and white matter maps, with age and sex as predictors. The 256 healthy individuals were used under 10-fold cross-validation to estimate the normative range, then the model trained on all 256 healthy individuals was applied to patients. A supplementary analysis used FreeSurfer-derived cortical thickness and pial area with the same 256 healthy individuals.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "This study also included 256 healthy individuals (mean [SD] age, 34 [9.5] years; 140 [54.7%] male)" "we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model trained on all data to patients."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are reported for the full healthy control group (n=256) used in the normative model. Mean age was 34 years (SD=9.5), with a range of 18-59 years, as reported in eTable 1. Since 10-fold cross-validation was used (no fixed train/test split), separate train-phase age statistics are not available.
